results.bound: \tilde{O}(D)\text{-round deterministic distributed algorithm; }\frac{3}{4}\text{-balanced path separator of size }O(D)\text{ when }T\text{ is a BFS tree}
results.previous_best: randomized \tilde{O}(D) rounds [Ghaffari-Parter DISC'17]; deterministic \tilde{O}(D) rounds [Jauregui et al. PODC'25]
results.quote: Theorem 1. Let G be an embedded planar graph of hop-diameter D, T be a spanning tree of G, and w(·) be a weight assignment to G’s vertices s.t. no vertex weighs more than 1/12 fraction of the total weight of G. There is a deterministic \tilde{O}(D)-round distributed algorithm that finds a u-to-v path P in T that is a 3/4-balanced separator of G. Adding the edge e=(u,v) to G (if it does not already exist), closes a fundamental cycle P∪{e} in T. Setting T to be a BFS tree produces a separator of size O(D).

results.problem: Distributed deterministic planar balanced separator in multiple vertex-disjoint subgraphs simultaneously
results.bound: \tilde{O}(D)\text{-round deterministic distributed algorithm; for each }G_i\text{, a }\frac{3}{4}\text{-balanced path separator of }O(\mathrm{depth}(T_i))\text{ vertices}
results.quote: Theorem 3. Let {G_i}_{i=1}^k be a partition of G into vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs, and {T_i}_{i=1}^k be spanning trees of G_i's. In addition let {w_i(·)}_{i=1}^k be 1/12-proper weight assignments to G_i's vertices. Then, there is a deterministic \tilde{O}(D)-round distributed algorithm that for each G_i finds a 3/4-balanced path separator P_i w.r.t. w_i(·) of O(depth(T_i)) vertices. In addition, P_i∪{e} is a fundamental cycle of T_i, where e=(u,v) and u,v are the endpoints of P. In case e∉G_i, then u,v learn the ID of each other, and a local ordering (embedding) of e that preserves planarity.
